date: 2026-10-08: E, pooling spectra by phase, object and group
lede: E is the next v5.0 step: Quantify on the spectrum summed over a phase, an object or a diffraction group, not only over a region you draw. The Core pieces exist and are tested, but nothing calls them yet. A draft registration raised 14 questions; these six cards are the ones only you can answer. Each has a recommendation and an independent second opinion (Haiku 5.5). Nothing is built until you answer; the parts no answer changes (sums, refusals, tests) may be built tonight without any on-screen surface.

cards.title: Build E in one step, or E1 first
context: ADR 061 lists E 'with H, I, K'. Pooled spectra (E1) need nothing new. H's outline, I (the channelling angle), K/dose and 'excess over the matrix' each need an input that does not exist yet: a misorientation function from the ACOM output, a probe current your files don't carry (Velox marks it uncalibrated, GMS writes 0), and a defined scale for subtracting the matrix (scaling by Al Kα would remove the signal it is meant to show).

Also worth knowing: the phase map is still badged unvalidated (one T4 metric failed on 2026-09-28). E1 is where its labels first become pooled counts that feed Quantify, so those results carry the same badge.

glossary.meaning: the exact sum of the spectra at a set of scan positions; counts stay counts.
the dossier's names: H = a 4D map masks the EDX map and back; I = channelling angle per pool; K = ζ-factor dose and thickness.

cards.question: E1 first, with H, I, K and excess as their own registrations?

options.label: E1 now; H, I, K and excess stay in v5.0 as separate registrations
options.what: Pooled spectra through the existing Quantify path, with refusals, badges and lineage. Each later piece is registered once its input exists, and is dropped from v5.0 if it can't.
options.effort: 2–3 sessions, plus a review and a drive
options.risk: low, provided the whole-map trap is fixed (a shapeless region is read as 'every pixel' today)

options.label: E1 now; H, I, K and excess move after v5.0
options.what: v5.0 ships pooling only; the other pieces wait for a later release.
options.risk: low; the scope is cut, which you sign here

options.label: All of E at once
options.what: Invent the three missing inputs first, each through its own Gate D.

cards.recommendWhy: E1 delivers the thing you asked for (Quantify per phase) without inventing inputs; the rest keeps its place in v5.0 and is decided on evidence.
cards.advisor: Agrees with a, at 2–3 sessions rather than 1–2. Name the whole-map fallthrough as the risk. Points out the sheet must ask whether v5.0 still ships H, I and K, hence option b.
sources: E draft: scratchpad E/prereg-draft.md (committed with the registration)

cards.title: How a single precipitate object is chosen
context: A real 4D window holds hundreds of precipitate objects; the Source picker becomes unusable above about 30 entries. ADR 061 names object pools, and mock v2.1 shows an 'object pool' entry.
cards.question: How do you pick one object to pool?

options.label: Pool by class in E1; single objects next, after a mock
options.what: All needles of a phase form the phase pool now. Single-object pooling follows as E1b once you've seen a mock of b or c.
options.risk: low; single objects come one step later

options.label: An object list: largest first, filtered by phase, '30 of 412'
options.what: In the Source picker or beside it.
options.effort: +1 session; new surface that needs a mock

options.label: Click an object on a map
options.what: Needs the 4D labels drawn over the room's EDX tiles.

cards.recommendWhy: No new surface lands before the drive, and a picture first is your rule; single objects stay in v5.0 as the next step.
cards.advisor: Disagrees: a, as written, cuts a named v5.0 item. Prefers b, a filterable list sorted by area that shows '30 of 412'. If you take a, sign that single objects come later.
cards.nothing: a; single objects are carded again with a mock.

cards.title: What the Source picker lists
context: Today the picker lists drawn regions and Whole map. With E it gains phases, and maybe diffraction groups.

glossary.meaning: positions grouped by pattern similarity in Crystal Maps (no phase claim).

cards.question: Which entries, in what layout, and what shows before a phase map exists?

options.label: Sectioned: Drawn · Whole map · Phases · Groups
options.what: With no phase map yet, one disabled line: 'Run phase mapping in Crystal Maps to pool by phase.'

options.label: Flat, phases only
options.what: No groups; nothing shown when there is no phase map.

options.label: Sectioned, with no empty-state line
options.what: As a, but silent until a phase map exists.

cards.recommendWhy: Sections keep a long list readable, and the line tells you why phases are missing instead of leaving you to guess.

cards.title: The positions the matcher did not index
context: Some scan positions get no phase. Their summed spectrum is what makes 'the phase pools add up to the whole map' visible, and it can show what the matcher missed.
cards.question: Show the not-indexed remainder, and how?

options.label: As a pool, 'Not indexed', badged unvalidated
options.what: Selectable like a phase, so it can be quantified.

options.label: As one line under the picker
options.what: 'Not indexed: 1 204 px, 3.1 % of counts'. A number only, no spectrum.

options.label: Not shown
options.risk: the pools silently don't add up

cards.recommendWhy: Its spectrum is useful scientifically (what failed to index), and it reconciles the pools with the whole map.
cards.advisor: Raised this as a separate decision. The draft's context calls the remainder 'an accounting number, not a pool'; if it is a pool, state its badge.

cards.title: When a 4D map may pool EDX pixels
context: The app can only state 'same scan': a GMS joint file with the same Experiment ID and an equal grid, mapped one to one. There is no lag check. ADR 053 (amended) names 'identity + lag check'. A phase map made on a strided or cropped view has a smaller grid than the spectrum image.

glossary.meaning: a measurement confirming the EDX and diffraction frames of each position came from the same probe position (no time offset).

cards.question: Is identity enough for simultaneous data, and what happens on a grid mismatch?

options.label: Identity for the same scan; refuse a mismatch with a sentence
options.what: Pools say 'same scan, identity; no lag check'. A mismatch reads: 'The phase map is 64 × 48; the spectrum image is 128 × 96. Run phase mapping on the full scan to pool by phase.'
options.risk: low; the missing check is stated, not hidden

options.label: As a, plus a typed scale/offset transform
options.effort: +1 session; new UI and a Gate D

options.label: Lag check first
options.what: Blocks E1 until a new measurement exists.

cards.recommendWhy: Simultaneous acquisition is the one case the app can state honestly; saying 'no lag check' keeps it honest.
cards.advisor: Agrees with a, reworded: 'registered: same run' claims more than the code checks; say 'same scan, identity; no lag check'. You should say whether identity suffices.

cards.title: Anything new drawn on screen in E1
context: H's first half, 'a 4D map masks the EDX map', could draw a pool's outline on the ColorMix. The other half (an EDX map masks the phase map) belongs in Crystal Maps. Extra numbers beside a pool (excess, f, dose, residual) have no picture yet. Every on-screen piece of E1 adds a row to 'Unverified on screen', and no further surface lands until a drive clears it.
cards.question: Does E1 draw anything new?

options.label: Nothing new
options.what: A pool behaves like a drawn region (spectrum, pixels · counts, Quantify, Compare, Pin); phase pools show the Phase row and the unvalidated badge.

options.label: Outline the pool's mask on the ColorMix

not_carded: Decided for you, overrule on sight: phase, object and 'Not indexed' pools carry the unvalidated badge because pools inherit their source's badge (the dossier rule). Group pools carry none because diffraction groups record no validation, and they are never called validated.
Decided for you: a pool whose source changes (a new phase map, new groups) is recomputed or removed, never shown stale.
footer: Sources: the E draft and its context (scratchpad E/, committed with the registration), ADR 053, ADR 061, the dossier. Second opinion: Haiku 5.5, read-only.
